title: Compare is not assign

blocks.md:
## `=` writes; `==` asks

A single `=` writes a new value onto a name. A double `==` asks whether two values are the same and answers with `True` or `False`. An `if` needs a question, not a write. `if flag == True:` asks. `if flag = True:` tries to assign in a place Python does not allow, so the file never becomes a running program.

This bites immediately: the starter will not even run. You get a syntax error before any print, so you never see `yes`. The line looks almost right, which makes the error feel mysterious until you notice the missing second equals sign.

```python
flag = True
if flag == True:
    print("yes")
```

A common mistake is leaving the assignment in the `if`, or deleting the test and printing `yes` with no condition. Either dodge skips the idea. The exercise asks you to fix the `if` so it asks whether `flag` is true. After the fix, the program should print `yes` and the source should contain `==`.

hintLadder.md: The error is about assignment in a place that wants a test.

description: Asking whether two things are equal is not the same as giving a name a value.
